title: Dualizing complex of a smooth proper curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $g:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] morphism of pure relative dimension one. Let $g^!$ denote the right adjoint of the derived pushforward $Rg_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] on quasi-coherent complexes. Then there is an isomorphism $g^!\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\cong\Omega^1_{C/k}[1]$ in the derived category of $\mathcal O_C$-modules, where $\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is the sheaf of relative Kähler differentials [def-sc-kahler-differentials].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-smooth-proper-relative-dualizing-general] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $X=C$, $f=g$, and $d=1$. The hypotheses match: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, and the given morphism is smooth and proper of pure relative dimension one. This gives $g^!\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\cong\Omega^1_{C/k}[1]$ since for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $X=C$ the sheaf $\Omega^1_{X/S}=\Delta^*(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)$ of the cited node is by definition the sheaf $\Omega^1_{C/k}$ of [def-sc-kahler-differentials].

For $d=1$, the first exterior power is the module itself, so $\Omega^1_{C/k}=\bigwedge^1\Omega^1_{C/k}$ by the defining property of the exterior algebra; the shift $[d]$ is therefore $[1]$. Rewriting the conclusion of Step 1 with these identities is exactly the displayed isomorphism.
